why_a_fourth_document: the rule file stays BYTE-UNCHANGED, as it has across all three prior companions. This one adds a measurement the rule does not contain, so appending it to the rule would make the rule's freeze timestamp cover text written after the arm was launched.

THE_DEFECT_THIS_EXISTS_TO_FIX.statement: the PRIMARY cannot distinguish two of its own four branches, because it is scored on a set the leak cannot act on.
THE_DEFECT_THIS_EXISTS_TO_FIX.the_mechanism_read_from_the_code_not_inf: scripts/glm_beyond_kmer.py::mg1655_candidate_sets builds `of` (the `orthology_free` pool) as `[w for w in held if (m.get(w.gene_id) or '') in only]` where `only = symbols(MG1655) - symbols(DRAFT_GFF)`. So every window in the PRIMARY's set is one whose GENE SYMBOL HAS NO COUNTERPART IN THE DRAFT ASSEMBLY. The scorer's own SET_STRAIN_NOTES says it outright: `eval genes have NO draft counterpart`.
THE_DEFECT_THIS_EXISTS_TO_FIX.why_that_is_fatal_to_the_branch_distinct: a near-ortholog leak is carried by the presence of a draft counterpart in training. On a set defined to EXCLUDE draft counterparts there is no near-ortholog to lose. Any cross-entropy change the representative model shows there is cross-ORGANISM cost (the corpus lost its only same-genus genome and 5.4% of its windows) plus trajectory noise. It is not the leak.
THE_DEFECT_THIS_EXISTS_TO_FIX.consequence: LEAK_WAS_REAL_AND_SMALL and CROSS_ORGANISM_COST_DOMINATES are BOTH consistent with any worse number on the primary set. The rule asks the primary to choose between them and the primary cannot.
THE_DEFECT_THIS_EXISTS_TO_FIX.the_yardstick_is_also_not_a_primary_set_: the +0.0054 the rule cites is `delta_model_bearing_minus_free` from wiki/glm_beyond_kmer_two_sets_2026-11-23.json -- a difference between the two OTHER sets. It was never a measurement on `orthology_free`.
THE_DEFECT_THIS_EXISTS_TO_FIX.and_the_yardstick_itself_is_unresolved: that contrast is graded UNRESOLVED_CONTRAST_SPANS_THE_MARGIN, and the same artifact's A_TENSION_RECORDED_RATHER_THAN_RESOLVED says its null-side figure (0.0100 nats on 120 windows) disagrees 14x with the better-powered all-window estimate (0.0007 nats) and instructs: `Do not quote either null-side figure as settled`. So the boundary between two branches rests on a number its own artifact says not to treat as settled.

THE_IDENTIFYING_MEASUREMENT_difference_i.quantity: DiD = (mean paired per-window delta on ortholog_bearing) - (mean paired per-window delta on withheld_orthology_free), where each per-window delta is `committed.left_only[i] - assessed.left_only[i]` (positive = the assessed model has LOWER cross-entropy = BETTER, per the sign correction)
THE_IDENTIFYING_MEASUREMENT_difference_i.why_this_identifies_the_leak: the two sets are both WITHHELD BY SEQUENCE and differ in exactly ONE property: whether the window's gene has a draft counterpart in training. `ortholog_bearing` = a - c and `withheld_orthology_free` = a & c in select_eval_windows, so they are DISJOINT halves of the same withheld pool at the same geometry and seed. Removing the draft removes the near-ortholog ONLY from the bearing half. Cross-organism cost acts on both halves, so it CANCELS in the difference. The DiD is therefore the leak-specific term.
THE_IDENTIFYING_MEASUREMENT_difference_i.this_is_the_same_contrast_the_two_sets_a: that artifact contrasted these two sets within ONE checkpoint. This contrasts the SAME two sets ACROSS checkpoints, which is what converts a correlational decomposition into a direct corpus-intervention measurement. The pairing is within-set across checkpoints; the between-set comparison is TWO-SAMPLE because the sets are disjoint.
THE_IDENTIFYING_MEASUREMENT_difference_i.statistic: two-sample percentile bootstrap on the two sets' per-window delta vectors, b and seed inherited from the run artifacts (boot 2000, seed = run_args.seed + 1), mirroring scripts/glm_two_set_contrast.py::two_sample_bootstrap
THE_IDENTIFYING_MEASUREMENT_difference_i.noise_floor_for_it: the identical DiD computed with the seed-1 reseed checkpoint in place of the representative one. Trajectory noise affects both halves, so its DiD should be near zero; a floor DiD comparable to the primary DiD means the design cannot resolve the leak at this sample size.
THE_IDENTIFYING_MEASUREMENT_difference_i.gate: the leak is reported as IDENTIFIED only if |DiD_primary| exceeds |DiD_floor| AND the DiD bootstrap CI excludes zero. Otherwise LEAK_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE_AT_THIS_SAMPLE_SIZE, and no leak size is quoted.

PRE_REGISTERED_EXPECTATION_with_a_magnit.direction: DiD_primary is expected NEGATIVE -- the representative model should lose MORE on the ortholog-bearing half than on the orthology-free half, because that is the half whose near-ortholog was removed.
PRE_REGISTERED_EXPECTATION_with_a_magnit.where_that_comes_from: the decomposition's delta_model_bearing_minus_free = +0.0054, i.e. the committed model was ABOUT that much better on the bearing half than on the free half. If that advantage was caused by the draft near-ortholog, removing the draft should erase it, so the DiD should land near -0.0054.
PRE_REGISTERED_EXPECTATION_with_a_magnit.what_a_near_zero_DiD_would_mean: the committed model's bearing-half advantage was NOT caused by the draft near-ortholog. That would make the +0.0054 decomposition a correlational artifact rather than a leak, and it would be a finding about the DECOMPOSITION, not a rescue of the model.
PRE_REGISTERED_EXPECTATION_with_a_magnit.what_a_much_larger_DiD_would_mean: the leak was bigger than the decomposition priced it. Recorded as a named possibility now so it cannot be presented later as the expected result.

HOW_IT_REPAIRS_THE_BRANCHES_without_edit.the_rule_s_branches_are_untouched: the four branches and the primary gate are computed exactly as frozen. This adds an ATTRIBUTION layer beside them, it does not replace them.
HOW_IT_REPAIRS_THE_BRANCHES_without_edit.what_the_grader_now_refuses_to_do: assert `branch_fit: CLEAN` on LEAK_WAS_REAL_AND_SMALL or CROSS_ORGANISM_COST_DOMINATES from the primary set alone. Without the two extra sets it stamps `attribution_identifiable: false` with the reason, because those two branches are not separable there.
HOW_IT_REPAIRS_THE_BRANCHES_without_edit.why_a_scoping_stamp_and_not_a_bar_change: stating that a design cannot distinguish two outcomes is a measurement fact about the design, established by reading the set-construction code. It is not a redefinition of the acceptance bar, and it does not move any threshold. Editing the rule's branch definitions after the arm was launched WOULD be a retro-fit, which is why that is not done here.
HOW_IT_REPAIRS_THE_BRANCHES_without_edit.cost: four additional scoring runs -- ortholog_bearing and withheld_orthology_free for each of the representative and reseed checkpoints. The committed checkpoint's two are ALREADY MEASURED and preserved at wiki/glm_beyond_kmer_runs_committed_2026-11-24/, so the committed arm costs nothing.

ORDERING_CLAIM.claim: written before ANY cross-entropy exists for either new checkpoint
ORDERING_CLAIM.what_was_true_when_this_was_written: the first representative attempt was killed at step 3500 and never scored; two relaunches were killed by machine crashes before step 500; no representative or reseed checkpoint has ever been scored on any set.
ORDERING_CLAIM.what_is_NOT_claimed: that the committed checkpoint's numbers on these sets are unknown. They are known, published, and preserved -- bearing -0.0248 and free -0.0094, which reproduce the two_sets artifact's -0.024778 and -0.009406 exactly. The expectation above is DERIVED from those committed numbers, which is legitimate because they predate this arm; what does not exist is any number from the arm itself.
ORDERING_CLAIM.verifiable_by: commit ordering -- this file and the grader that implements it are committed before any run artifact for either new checkpoint exists.

honest_limits: The DiD cancels cross-organism cost only to the extent that it acts EQUALLY on both halves. If the bearing half is systematically easier or harder in some way correlated with having a draft counterpart, that difference does not cancel. The two halves are not randomised -- they are defined by a biological property.
Both halves are 120-window samples of their pools, so the DiD carries the sampling variation of two subsamples, not one. Its CI will be wider than the primary's.
The reseed floor remains ONE draw of trajectory noise, now applied to a difference of two differences, so it is a noisier point estimate than the primary's floor.

A resolved DiD prices the leak for THIS corpus change, which removed an entire genome. It does not isolate the near-ortholog contribution from the loss of that genome's other 3,463 windows, because both happened in the same intervention.
None of this produces a same-strain beyond-k-mer verdict. The representative corpus has no E. coli at all, so the model remains a cross-organism generator.
